blocks.text:
Breakfast and check out.

We head west until we reach San Javier.

San Javier is a Russian colony located in the northwest of the Río Negro department, on the banks of the Uruguay River.

The town was built from a process of immigration of 300 Russian families who arrived in the area in 1913.

Along with their leader, Basilio Lubkov, they occupied the hectares granted by the then Minister of Development and Agriculture, José Espalter, to inhabit and work on.

Here you will be able to meet local people and discover stories of life and overcoming challenges.

Free time to explore, then continue heading to Fray Bentos to spend the night.

Accommodation in Fray Bentos.

blocks.text:
Breakfast, check out and visit Anglo Museum

This is one of the main attractions our department offers to tourists, where much of the history of the departmental capital remains alive. This museum, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site, show us the history and memories of the former Liebig salting plant (1863) and the Anglo Uruguay Refrigerator, which operated until 1979. It is an essential reference site for local history and identity, boasting an industrial heritage of international significance. Lunch included in a local restaurant inside Anglo facilities. Departure from Fray Bentos to Colonia del Sacramento.

This City was founded in 1680 by the Portuguese, the city transitioned from Portuguese to Spanish ruling for over a century. These events turned the Historic Quarter of the Colonia capital into a melting pot of architectural and urban styles, where typically Portuguese colonial styles coexist with Spanish-style residences. It is due to this unique combination in its urban landscape that the historic center of Colonia del Sacramento has been designated by UNESCO as a Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Enjoy a tour of the cobbled Historic Quarter, which will allow you to delve into the history and approach the city's rich cultural heritage. Museums, theater, art, crafts, and good cuisine complement a range of possibilities for visitors. The memorable walking tour will take you to the famous Street of Sighs, the Church of the Holy Sacrament, the Bastion of San Pedro, the Powder House (former ammunition depot), the lighthouse, the Portuguese, Spanish, and tile museums (admissions not included).

At the end of this visit transfer to Colonia´s Pier to take your ferry to Buenos Aires. End of our services.
